# Migration from v1.x to v2.x

If you're asking yourself if and how you should plan the migration, you will find some information on this page about what changed, has been renamed or deprecated.

## General

### Minimal react version

We dropped support for react v16 and now only support react v17 and v18.

In the future we plan to follow react major release cycles with major release of our library, deprecating legacy react versions.

If you need to maintain a react v16 codebase, React maintainers provide long term security support for v16 to v18 (see https://endoflife.date/react) and we will support critical fixes in v1.x of our react library.

### Opt in global CSS Styles

Global css styles are now optional.

To use them, you can either apply a `ds-styles` class to any html element or use the <LinkTo kind="Components/Typography" story="basic">Typography</LinkTo> component.

<div className="sbdocs-compare">
  <Source
    code={`// v1.x
<h3>My title</h3>
`}
    language="jsx"
  />
  <Source
    code={`// v2.x with ds-styles class
<body className="ds-styles"><h3>My Title</h3></body>
// v2.x with Typography component
<body><Typography variant="h3">My title</Typography></body>
`}
    language="jsx"
  />
</div>

## Typings

We improved typings by following the 3 principles below
- Re-export third party library types used by our components
- Export custom prop types
- Prefix prop types with component name

### Types imports

The types below where already available as direct imports in v1, but have been renamed in v2.

| v1 type   | v2 type          | Infos                                                                |
| --------- | ---------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Placement | PopoverPlacement | See <LinkTo kind="Components/Popover" story="basic">Popover</LinkTo> |

The types below where either not exported or available by importing them from the full path, or from 3rd party libraries types.
In v2 they are available as direct imports.

| v1 type (full path or 3rd party)     | v2 type                      | Infos                                                                |
| ------------------------------------ | ---------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| (ComboBox path)/DefaultOption        | ComboBoxDefaultOption        | See <LinkTo kind="Components/ComboBox" story="basic">Combo Box</LinkTo> |
| (ComboBox path)/VirtualizationOption | ComboBoxVirtualizationOption | |
| n/a                                  | ComboBoxGetOptionProperty    | |
| (DataTable path)/Column              | DataTableColumnDef           | See <LinkTo kind="Components/DataTable" story="basic">Data Table</LinkTo> |
| (DataTable path)/SelectionMode       | DataTableSelectionMode       | |
| react-table/CellContext              | DataTableCellContext         | |
| react-table/ExpandedState            | DataTableExpandedState       | |
| react-table/Row                      | DataTableRow                 | |
| react-table/RowData                  | DataTableRowData             | |
| react-table/SortingState             | DataTableSortingState        | |
| n/a                                  | createColumnHelper           | |
| n/a                                  | DataTableExpandableOptions   | |
| n/a                                  | DataTableQuery               | |
| n/a                                  | DataTableState               | |
| (Footer path)/LinkOption             | FooterLinkOption             | See <LinkTo kind="Components/Footer" story="basic">Footer</LinkTo> |
| (Select path)/SelectOption           | SelectOption                 | See <LinkTo kind="Components/Select" story="basic">Select</LinkTo> |

### Deprecated types from @airbus/elements

In v1, `@airbus/elements` sources included types that were imported into react codebase.

**Projects impacted by this are those who copy pasted our react components code in their own codebase.**

For example

- [Button props type](https://github.airbus.corp/Airbus/design-system/blob/270fa437f3b58b4429ed967e7fb0c0c68bb1ac9c/packages/elements/src/elements/Button/index.ts#L4) in @airbus/elements codebase
- [Type import](https://github.airbus.corp/Airbus/design-system/blob/6839a390db8e4582d720f5e5320d32f72a1c78c9/packages/components-react/src/components/Button/Button.tsx#L9) in @airbus/components-react codebase

We initially envisionned to generate components for various frameworks based on these generic typed props.
This has never been achieved and these types were polluting the codebase with unneeded complexity.

## Components

### Data Table

We migrated from `react-table` to `@tanstack/react-table` internally.<br />
The main impact of this is that **column definition format has changed**.
see <LinkTo kind="Components/DataTable" story="basic">Data Table</LinkTo>.

#### Column Definitions

- `accessor` was replaced by `accessorKey` or `accessorFn` (depending on whether you are using a string or function)
- `width`, `minWidth`, `maxWidth` where renamed to `size`, `minSize`, `maxSize`
- Optionally, you can use the new `createColumnHelper` function (See <LinkTo kind="Components/DataTable" story="cells">Cells example</LinkTo>)
  around each column definition for better TypeScript hints. (You can still just use an array of column definitions)
  - The first parameter is the accessor key or accessor function
  - The second parameter is an object of column options
- cell and header `value` parameter was replaced by `getValue` getter
  (to improve performance by evaluating the value only when getValue() is called and caching the result)

<div className="sbdocs-compare">
  <Source
    code={`// v1.x
const columns = [
  {
    accessor: "name",
    Header: "Full Name",
    width: 300,
    minWidth: 100,
    maxWidth: 400,
    Cell: ({ value }) => (value ? value : "-"),
  }
]`}
    language="jsx"
  />
  <Source
    code={`// v2.x
const columns = [
  {
    accessorKey: "name",
    // or using a function
    // accessorFn: (row) => row.name || row.pseudo,
    header: "Full Name",
    size: 300,
    minSize: 100,
    maxSize: 400,
    cell: ({ getValue }) => (getValue() ? getValue() : "-"),
  }
]`}
    language="jsx"
  />
</div>

### Select

#### Default mode

The default mode for the `Select` component has been changed from `NATIVE` to `AUTO`.
In `AUTO` mode, the component will have a custom and consistent UI on all os and browsers,
and switch to native html `select` on touch devices.

You can control how the component switch from one mode to another by managing the `mode` prop.

See <LinkTo kind="Components/Select" story="Modes">Select modes</LinkTo>

<div className="sbdocs-compare">
  <Source
    code={`// v1.x : default to native html select
<Select options={options}></Select>`}
    language="jsx"
  />
  <Source
    code={`// v2.x : default to custom html + native on touch screens
<Select options={options}></Select>`}
    language="jsx"
  />
</div>

#### Readonly input

In custom mode, the Select component reuse the ComboBox internally, based on an input and a popover.

In v1, this allowed to use the input element of the ComboBox to type text, filter options, etc.

In v2, the input html element will be readonly. If you need all the features of the ComboBox, please use this component instead.

<div className="sbdocs-compare">
  <Source
    code={`// v1.x : editable input
<Select options={options}></Select>`}
    language="jsx"
  />
  <Source
    code={`// v2.x : readonly input
<Select options={options}></Select>`}
    language="jsx"
  />
</div>

### Combobox

There is no breaking change in terms of API, and your code will work out of the box.
But we improved management of aria labelling for screen readers.

#### Aria labelling

Downshift library adds by default an `aria-labelledby` attribute to the `input` html element of the Combobox.
This is meant to reference the id of the html label displaying a title on top of the Combobox.
But the component can be used without a visible label, resulting in broken aria attributes.
The correct approach in this case is to provide an `aria-label` attribute to give screen readers information on the purpose of the component.

The component now supports both `aria-label` and `aria-labelledby` attributes.
To make your life simpler, if a `placeholder` attribute is passed, it will also set `aria-label` with the same value.

<div className="sbdocs-compare">
  <Source
    code={`// v1.x
<ComboBox placeholder="Choose a language" />
// renderred input (NOK: "combobox-1-label" does not exist)
<input
  placeholder="Choose a language"
  aria-labelledby="combobox-1-label">
`}
    language="jsx"
  />
  <Source
    code={`// v2.x
<ComboBox placeholder="Choose a language" />
// renderred input (OK)
<input
  placeholder="Choose a language"
  aria-label="Choose a language">
`}
    language="jsx"
  />
</div>

You can now also set aria attributes yourself

<Source
  code={`
<ComboBox placeholder="Languages" aria-label="Choose a language" />
<ComboBox placeholder="Languages" aria-labelledby="my-label-id" />
// renderred inputs
<input placeholder="Languages" aria-label="Choose a language">
<input placeholder="Languages" aria-labelledby="my-label-id">
`}
  language="jsx"
/>

We also updated the <LinkTo kind="Components/FormControl" story="basic">FormControl</LinkTo> component to automatically provide the correct `aria-labelledby` attribute based on the `label` prop.

<Source
  code={`
<FormControl label="Languages" placeholder="Choose a language">
  <ComboBox />
</FormControl>
// renderred input ("FormControl-358-label" is the right id of the label)
<input aria-labelledby="FormControl-358-label" placeholder="Choose a language">
`}
  language="jsx"
/>

### Accordion

In v1 all collapsible items grow by default to fit available height.<br />
In v2 you can choose which collapsible items will grow by using the `autoFit` prop.
See <LinkTo kind="Components/Accordion" story="max-height">Accordion</LinkTo>

<div className="sbdocs-compare">
  <Source
    code={`// v1.x - all Collapsible items will grow
<div className="h-480">
  <Accordion>
    <Collapsible title="Title 1">Item 1</Collapsible>
    <Collapsible title="Title 2">
      Item with lot of text
    </Collapsible>
  </Accordion>
</div>
`}
    language="jsx"
  />
  <Source
    code={`// v2.x - only second item will grow
<div className="h-480">
  <Accordion>
    <Collapsible title="Title 1">Item 1</Collapsible>
    <Collapsible title="Title 2" autoFit>
      Item with lot of text
    </Collapsible>
  </Accordion>
</div>
`}
    language="jsx"
  />
</div>
